origin.description: Return the start and end of the first match in each string. The positions are inclusive, so a zero-length match has an end smaller than its start.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A plain character vector is a regular expression. fixed compares literal text, coll uses collation, and boundary matches character, word, line, or sentence boundaries. The empty string is a character boundary.

origin.details: The inputs follow vctrs recycling: a length-1 vector is repeated, including down to length 0, and any other disagreeing lengths are an error. Names on string are copied onto the rows when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string. The empty pattern and boundary() both locate boundary segments. A miss is a row of missing positions.
origin.value: An integer matrix with columns start and end, and one row for each element of string or pattern. Positions are 1-based and inclusive.

translation.description: Return the start and end of the first match in each string. The positions are inclusive, so a zero-length match has an end smaller than its start.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list is an ICU regular expression. fixed, coll, regex, and boundary return Pattern objects and select that engine. The empty string is a character boundary.

translation.details: check_lengths raises RecycleError when lengths other than 0 and 1 disagree. pattern_type chooses the engine and pattern_opts supplies the stringi option list. Empty and bound both call stri_locate_first_boundaries. Fixed, collation, and regex call the matching stri_locate_first function. A miss is NA, NA. Names on string are kept when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string.
translation.value: A list of [start, end] rows. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. A missing position is stringi._na.NA, which is JSON null.
translation.example:
from stringr.locate import str_locate
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
print(str_locate(fruit, "a"))
